Drew.note: I'm Farm with the Kookaburra this round. I'll visit Blair, who was the most suspicious player in the last round, to learn their role.

Ellis.note: As the Tit I gain only if my guessed role is right. Finley's Round 1 read named Blair as the Mouser, so I'll visit Blair and guess Mouser.

Finley.note: I'm Eagle again and need to visit someone. Drew is the leader and the most suspicious player, so I'll visit Drew to learn their visitors.

Alex.feeling: Round 3 is tangled: Blair is the leading suspect, but Drew's confused Kookaburra report and Ellis's collapse leave the picture murky, so I'm wary of voting on thin evidence.

Blair.feeling: I'm the Mouser and about to be eggsecuted on Ellis's Tit accusation and the table's pile-on, so the round feels precarious and I'm mostly reacting to who's pushing hardest.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled, with conflicting claims and a Wink possibly in play.

Drew.feeling: Messy and confusing: my confused dawn report makes my own read unreliable, and Ellis's collapse plus conflicting visit stories have the table pointing at Blair.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and murky: I was eliminated early on a Wink, and the table's claims conflict enough that I can't verify most of them.

Finley.feeling: Tense and confusing: the claims clash, one player is already dead, and the throw on Blair rests on a single Tit read.

Alex.note: Blair is the consensus throw and I'm Farm. I'll throw W5 and H3 to vote without risking my high cards.

Blair.note: Casey is out, but Alex, Finley and Drew still lean on me, so I'm likely eggsecuted. I'll throw my lowest card at Drew, a Farm player, so my highest card comes back if we lose.

Casey.note: The table has converged on Blair. I'll throw my two lowest-value cards at Blair.

Drew.note: Blair is the consensus target, and I'll throw one 13 to keep risk low while still adding a vote.

Ellis.note: I'm dead, so my throws don't count as votes, but they bank at full value if Farm wins. My Tit read on Blair as Mouser is a confirmed egg, so I'm confident. I'll throw my high cards at Blair and keep the Wild and the 1.

Finley.note: Blair is the agreed target and the best-supported Meowfia read, so I throw three low cards at Blair to add weight to the vote.

Alex.confusing: Eagle's mechanic was easy to misread: I wrongly argued it counted visitors to the Eagle itself, and that cost me credibility when Finley's +3 was correct. The 6-6 tie rule also surprised me, since a Farm player was eliminated even though Meowfia was tied with them.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when Blair's Farm story collapsed under the Hawk and Kookaburra claims and the table converged on the Mouser. Finley's last-words accusation before collapsing was a satisfying read.
Alex.change: I'd make the Eagle and similar visitor-count roles state explicitly whose nest they count, so early claims don't turn into arguments about the rules.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I disputed Finley's correct Eagle read and called a vote on Drew, which split the table and let a 6-6 tie eliminate me. Next time I'd check the rule before challenging a claim and keep my throw count from creating a tie.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle rule was unclear: whether it counts visitors to the Eagle or to its target caused the biggest dispute in round 2. Dawn reports for confused players were also hard to trust.
Blair.fun: Learning as the Sphinx that Alex was the only Hawk, which exposed Drew's false Hawk claim. Winking a player right after they named me as the Mouser was also satisfying.
Blair.change: State the Eagle's visitor count explicitly in the role text, and add a clear note on how confused reports work.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I publicly called out Drew's Hawk claim, which revealed my Sphinx information and made the table turn on Drew. I'd keep that quiet and steer the vote toward Alex more quietly.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count caused the most argument: I first thought it counted visitors to the Eagle itself, and only later did the table settle on counting visitors to its target. Confused dawn reports also made it hard to know which claims to trust.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: my Eagle visit to Blair showed Drew and Finley as visitors, which exposed Blair as Meowfia. Watching the Mouser's Wink and the collapses shape the table was also engaging.
Casey.change: Make the Eagle rule and visitor-counting wording unambiguous so players spend less time arguing over it. A clearer confusion notice would also help.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I wavered between Alex and Blair and cast my throw at Blair while the table split, so Alex was eggsecuted instead. I should have committed to one suspect earlier and pressed it with the others.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle counts visitors to its target, not to itself, and the table argued about that for a whole day. Being confused also made my dawn report unreliable, so I couldn't trust the Kookaburra result.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was fun: I was Floofer, and my Meowfia partner Blair was never found, so the table voted out Alex, a Farm player, while we won the round.
Drew.change: I'd make it clearer when a nest changes because of someone else's visit versus a player's own action, since the Eagle and Falcon claims kept getting mixed up.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw only one 13 at Blair, but a winning throw banks it at full value, so I should have thrown two 13s; that's about 12 points I left behind, and I finished 2 points behind Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle counting rule was confusing: Finley's +3 and Alex's rebuttal showed how easily the table argued over whether it counts visitors to the Eagle or to its target. Nobody could verify the Kookaburra's confused report either.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: the table converged on Blair as the Mouser, and Finley's Kookaburra read plus my Tit guess formed a real lead. Winning that round's throw was satisfying.
Ellis.change: I would make dawn reports more verifiable, for example by revealing who visited whom to the target's role, so claims like Eagle counts and Kookaburra confusion are easier to check.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I joined the push on Drew after clearing Alex too quickly, and I threw two 8s into a losing vote. I should have pressed harder on Alex's Hawk story and checked Drew's Floofer claim before throwing.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's gain counts visitors to the player it visits, not to the Eagle itself, and I briefly saw other players misread that. The Tit and Kookaburra reports were also hard to check when players were confused.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: my Kookaburra read named Blair as the Mouser, and the table threw at Blair as the Meowfia. Ellis and Drew then pushed the vote together with me.
Finley.change: I'd make the Eagle's rule clearer on the card, since it's easy to misread the visitor count as visitors to the Eagle.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I announced my Kookaburra read and visit on day one, which exposed me and got me collapsed by Blair's Wink. I should have held the reveal until the vote.
